summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and recurrent tracheitis was admitted for persistent productive cough, green tracheal secretions, chest pain with coughing, and new-onset watery diarrhea. A chest X-ray showed clear lungs, and sputum culture revealed sparse growth of MRSA and Pseudomonas aeruginosa with white blood cells, indicating active infection. She was started on IV vancomycin and switched to oral ciprofloxacin based on sensitivities. Her symptoms improved during the hospital stay. She was discharged home with a plan to complete 7 days of IV vancomycin and 14 days of oral ciprofloxacin, along with follow-up for iron deficiency anemia and coordination of care with pulmonology, ENT, and primary care. Social work follow-up was recommended to address psychosocial needs.
problems: Methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection, unspecified site
